question: On SEEDK's knot-local fills, is the far-pair sign (the far end pair separated by every crossed split) exactly SEED's copy step, and do F1, T1 and T2 hold; does the copy class's betweenness read the sign?

definitions.sign: every crossed split separates c from d (far end knot B(c,d,r))
definitions.weak sign: r sides with d on every crossed split
definitions.near-pair sign: no crossed split separates the near pair {a,p}
definitions.F1: a fill giving an uncrossed split a crossing has the sign
definitions.T1: under the sign no uncrossed split is moved
definitions.T2: under the sign the moved crossed splits are one whole order
definitions.pattern: L6: every crossed split separates p from q, none separates a from p, some but not all separate p from d
definitions.marked picture: closure picture plus each split's trace on (p;q,a,c,d) and a crossed mark

forbidden_inputs: Changing the starts, readings, predictions, coverage or decision rules after seeing registered results
cheapest_meaningful_control: The library's SEED verdict equals knotlib's on every extension; L1, L2, K1 on every treated knot set.

predictions.R0: every copy step has a treated knot set; every crossing-making knot set of the shape pins r to the shared distinction
predictions.R1: sign = copy step on every crossing-making extension
predictions.R2: F1 on every treated knot set
predictions.R3: T1 and T2 under the sign
predictions.R4: L6 pattern on every treated set of every copy step and none of a refused fill
predictions.R5: weak sign and near-pair sign each = copy step
predictions.R6: every treated set in state alpha or beta; no fill with both
predictions.R7: (i) both verdicts in the copy class; (ii) no marked picture with both verdicts

decision_rules.R1: no exception either way; every exception printed
decision_rules.coverage: >= 100 sign sets with smaller order >= 3 or R3 untested there; copy steps with p an earlier r and with >= 2 earlier copy steps counted
decision_rules.harness: L1/L2/K1 or the SEED cross-check failing is a bug and stops the read-out

stop_rule: One run; referee hand-off; report; the two-order line stops.
